notes.meaning: David asks the Lord who is allowed to come near and live in His presence. In David's time, God's place of worship was a holy tent in Jerusalem. To stay as a guest in God's tent means enjoying His daily protection, care, and friendship.

differ.view: The tent represents the church on earth, because a tent is temporary and does not describe heaven.
The tent and the holy hill point beyond earthly worship to entering heaven itself.
The tent pictures faithful worshipers in the church on earth, while the holy mountain pictures the church triumphant in heaven.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine saw the tent as a soldier's temporary camp, picturing a believer's battle against the devil while finding shelter in Christ.

notes.meaning: The Lord answers by describing someone whose everyday life is honest and pure. Walking with integrity means living out God's ways in every part of life, not just when others are watching. This person does what is right and always speaks the truth straight from an honest heart.

differ.view: Upright actions do not earn right standing with God, but are the outward fruit of faith in Christ's righteousness.
God requires actual obedience in daily conduct, because only those who live out the law are accepted by Him.

notes.meaning: A godly person refuses to use words to harm other people. The picture here is of someone who refuses to go around spreading hurtful gossip or ruining a neighbor's good name. True friends will not invent evil reports, nor will they listen to rumors or pass them along.

A citizen of God's kingdom judges people by God's standards rather than by money or fame. Such a person does not flatter open wickedness, but honors anyone who loves and obeys the Lord. Even when keeping a solemn promise brings personal loss or hardship, this person stays faithful and keeps their word.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Ancient Greek and Latin translations, followed by the Douay-Rheims, understand the final line as swearing to one's neighbor without deceit rather than keeping a costly oath.

notes.meaning: The psalm warns against taking unfair advantage of neighbors who are in need, especially by charging greedy interest on loans. It also forbids accepting bribes that harm innocent people in court. Anyone who lives with such honesty and mercy rests safely in God and will never be torn away from His presence.

differ.view: The promise of never being shaken means a true believer will persevere to the end and never be permanently cast away.
Believers remain secure in God's favor only as long as they continue walking faithfully in good works.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view the promise of never being shaken as meaning continuous security and outward stability under divine protection in this life.
